To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a specification logic for assertion based simulation based verification that incorporates timing, data and allows for a succinct assertion specification.

We have developed a logic for assertion based formal verification which allows us, to (a) represent assertions succinctally, (b) incorporate data-orientaion and (c) associate timing in the design intentions.

(i) we have defined a new logic called TAB logic for representing design intentions, (ii) we have shown how TAB logic can be used for assertion based verification and (iii) we have presented results of applying TAB logic for verification of a complex real time system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a specification language for assertion based verification and algorithms to check assertions on a simulation trace.
the development of efficient techniques for verification of complex real time embedded systems.
the development of a specification logic which can be used for verification and synthesis of complex real time embedded systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the work described in this thesis is a contribution towards formalizing the specification of real time systems and their verification using temporal logic based assertions.
TAB logic is a powerful specification logic which allows us to incorporate data-orientation, timing, and abstraction.
the work in this thesis is an attempt to address the problem of formal verification in a systematic manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TAB logic can be used as a high level assertion language for verification and simulation.
TAB logic can be used as a specification language for high level design verification, and as a specification logic for high level synthesis.
we have developed a new logic, which allows us to represent assertions in a compact and intuitive manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed logic is expressive, compact and efficient.
the use of temporal logic in the verification process can be made more effective by associating timing information with the design intent.
the proposed logic can be used to express design intentions at a higher level of abstraction and can be verified on simulation traces of a low level implementation.
